headline: A Kingfisher Answered Her Prayer—and Landed on Her Hand
meta_description: A park ranger in Somerset asked for a sign, and moments later a shy Eurasian kingfisher landed on her gloved hand and stayed for 10 minutes.
summary_short: Laura O'Brien, a 24-year-old park ranger in Somerset, asked for a sign—and a kingfisher immediately appeared and perched on her hand for 10 minutes.
body:
Laura O'Brien, a 24-year-old park maintenance ranger for the Frome Town Council in Somerset, had just asked for a sign when the answer arrived in an unexpected form. Moments later, a brilliant blue Eurasian kingfisher streaked through the air, flew directly toward her, and landed on her gloved hand—where it remained for a full 10 minutes. "It was such a magical moment that I will never forget," she told SWNS news. "I felt like Snow White!" The encounter left her amazed, since kingfishers are notoriously shy and elusive birds, typically glimpsed only as a flash of blue before they vanish. This one stayed long enough for her to admire its bright orange chest up close while she stood watering flowers at her workplace.

What made the moment even more remarkable was how it unfolded. Concerned the bird might be injured as it darted nearby, Laura held out her hand as an offering of help. The kingfisher immediately hopped on, seemingly content to rest there. "So I was just watering the flowers with this kingfisher on my finger," she recalled, still in disbelief at the unlikely scene she'd captured on video.

When Laura shared the encounter with her fellow rangers back at the Frome Town Council, their reaction was unanimous: jealousy. The bird eventually flew back down to the river from which it had come, leaving Laura with a memory most birdwatchers spend lifetimes hoping to experience. She's already considering returning to the river to see if her feathered visitor might recognize her. For someone who asked the universe for a sign, the answer could hardly have been more vivid—or more gentle.
quick_facts: Kingfisher perched on her gloved hand for 10 minutes
Eurasian kingfisher known for being shy and elusive
She asked for a sign moments before it appeared
Bright orange chest visible during rare close encounter
